The controller never buys grid energy for such a row. At 100 % SOC it follows CHARGE_PV (0 A in Capacity mode, the cap in Voltage mode) and it raises no warning. The threshold is the 0.000001 kWh the plan's own classifier reads as zero: the plan publishes the solver's flows unrounded, and a CURTAIL row that does not charge can carry up to about 5e-13 kWh there (about one such row in twelve in the sweep of ADR-0005), which must not charge. Any other CURTAIL row (charge_kwh up to 0.000001 kWh) runs the HOLD profile with the warning CURTAIL is not supported: HOLD applied, because the controller cannot limit PV: it holds the pack by the TOU floor (below) and writes the larger of hold_grid_current (1 A by default) and min_buffer_current as the charge current.

HOLD does not buy energy: the program stays active in direction Grid, the grid current is 0 A and the target is the lower of the planned end SOC (rounded down) and the level the pack has now. A floor above the live SOC would make the inverter charge from the grid, so the target never exceeds the level read when the hold began; that level (SOC and voltage) is latched in the runtime while the state stays HOLD or CURTAIL, so the target does not creep with the SOC and does not rewrite the TOU entities on every percent. The discharge current is the discharge cap, so the battery carries the house while the floor is above it. CHARGE_GRID writes the discharge cap too, instead of 0 A, so a house load that appears during a grid charge is served by the battery and not pushed to the grid.

Only battery modes listed in commissioned_battery_modes are controlled; any other mode (for example Voltage before its thresholds were proven) keeps the base profile. With Voltage allowed, a target outside 495–560 V is refused.

With the counter SOC estimator as the SOC source the controller reads its SOC from the estimator instead of the Solarman battery entity (the telemetry gate, the Voltage-mode full-pack rule and the reached checks), and Capacity is dropped from the modes it controls, whatever commissioned_battery_modes says: in Capacity mode the inverter compares the programs' SOC thresholds with its own BMS SOC, so the plan's target would be in the wrong scale. The inverter then stays on the base profile with mode_not_commissioned if it is switched to Capacity.

In Voltage mode the pack voltage sags under discharge (about 0.7 V at 7 kW) and the LFP curve is flat (515–528 V spans roughly 30–70 %), so a DISCHARGE_GRID voltage target is reached within seconds of starting. With a numeric discharge_energy_entity, a DISCHARGE_GRID interval in Voltage mode instead ends once the counter has risen by the planned discharge_kwh (0.05 kWh tolerance) since the controller's first run in that interval (runtime.slot_energy); the TOU program voltage is then 49.6 (496 V), so the inverter only stops on its own at that floor. Solarman reports the counter only when it changes, so its freshness comes from the telemetry_entities heartbeat of the same inverter. Without a numeric counter the voltage target applies as before. Capacity mode is unchanged.

Charging lifts the pack voltage the other way: about 2 V at 4 A within seconds, and the inverter stops grid charging as soon as the pack reaches the TOU voltage. A CHARGE_GRID target from the curve (51.4 V for 27 % at a 512 V rest voltage) therefore ended the charge after a few seconds, and a rest voltage above the curve point latched the interval as reached at once. In Voltage mode CHARGE_GRID (outside a balance row) writes voltage_grid_charge_ceiling (55.2 V, 552 V) as the TOU voltage instead; the planned grid current sets how much each interval charges, and the interval is reached only when the pack reaches the ceiling. The Solarman charge counter refreshes about every 10 minutes, too slowly to end a 15-minute interval, so it is not used. Keep the ceiling at or below the BMS charge voltage limit.

Grid outage

When the grid is out the battery is the only source of the house. The plan no longer describes anything the inverter can do, and a battery limit of 0 A (what the blueprint writes in HOLD) would cut the house off. Energy Compass therefore watches the grid, with the controller enabled, on both engines. The BACKUP state and the writes below are native-engine only.

Step What happens
Source the grid_presence_entity option, else the device's Solarman grid binary sensor (on = present); when it is not readable, the phase voltages: grid_voltage_entities, else grid_l1_voltage, grid_l2_voltage and grid_l3_voltage. Every numeric phase under 100 V means absent, any phase at 100 V or more present. An unreadable source keeps the last known state
Enter the grid must be absent without a break for outage_enter_seconds (15 s by default, 5–600); the binary sensor grid_outage turns on
During the controller runs BACKUP; the planner does not solve (below); the notification says so (see Outage messages)
Leave the grid must be present without a break for outage_stable_minutes (5 min by default, 1–120); a break starts the wait again. restored_pending_since on the sensor shows when it began
After the retained plan is followed until the planner has published a fresh one, which it does at once

BACKUP writes both battery currents at their caps, grid charging at 0 A, all six programs Disabled, SOC 10 %, 49.6 (496 V) and the power max_power_w, whatever the plan says (even with no plan). The runtime code is ok, reason_code is grid_outage and confirmed_mode is BACKUP. The writes are their own phase: the discharge limit first (the battery must be free to feed the house), then charge, then grid charging, then the program selects, then the rest; no write lowers a current, and the protective stop before a profile change skips the battery limits while the grid is out. The stop that remains writes min_buffer_current, never 0 A.

Condition Result
Mode Auto BACKUP is written
Mode Simulation BACKUP is computed and shown in the runtime, nothing is written
Mode Off, the pause switch on hands off, as always
Telemetry stale, the six TOU start times not different and rising, or a battery mode other than Capacity or Voltage the base profile, as without an outage (telemetry_stale, tou_times, operation_mode)

The planner holds too. While the grid is out it starts no solve, whatever changes (inputs, settings, the interval boundary, a restart): the status is calculating with the reason grid_outage, the last plan stays on the plan sensor with plan_retained set, and no Alert is raised. When the outage ends the status changes to calculating with the reason grid_restored and a solve starts at once. A Home Assistant restart in the middle of an outage restores the watch from the store, so it does not solve either.

The grid watch is saved in the controller store, so a restart keeps an outage that is running. Two limits: with the controller disabled nothing watches the grid, and the blueprint writes 0 A in HOLD. Rolling back to the blueprint engine (or running the blueprint automation) therefore loses the outage safety: no BACKUP, and a held pack can be cut off from the house. The binary sensor, the planner hold and the notifications stay.

Writes and confirmation

Each change writes one entity through number.set_value or select.select_option, then reads holding registers 108–177 from the controller's Solarman device (device_id) and compares the raw value. A register that does not confirm is listed in runtime.uncertain and retried; a direction or target change first lowers the currents to min_buffer_current, then sets thresholds, then enables the direction.

Runtime code Meaning
waiting the first run has not published a code yet
ok the planned profile is computed (Simulation) or written and confirmed (Auto)
blocked no valid plan or a gate failed; reason and reason_code say which
restored the base profile was written and confirmed (release in Off, or no valid plan in Auto)
verification_required writes finished but not every register confirmed
write_failed a register did not confirm after retries; restore stays pending
simulation_blocked Simulation was refused while a restore was pending
paused the pause switch is on (native engine): the decision is computed, nothing is written
error the run itself failed (native engine): an exception, or Energy Compass or the Solarman entities could not be read; reason_code is run_failed or controller_unavailable. After three failed runs in a row the repair issue "Deye controller runs are failing" appears; the next good run clears both

runtime.reason_code is a stable code and runtime.reason its text. The native engine writes the text in the Home Assistant language (Polish for pl, English otherwise); the blueprint engine's texts are Polish.

reason_code Meaning
ok nothing blocks the plan
telemetry_stale telemetry entities not numeric or older than 30 s, voltage outside 400–610 V or SOC outside 0–100 %
tou_times the six TOU start times are not different and rising
session_wait no plan accepted yet in this session
plan_revoked the accepted generation was revoked after an error
grid_outage the grid is out and the state is BACKUP: both currents at their caps, grid charge 0 A, every program Disabled
plan_sources an Alert is on or the publication is not ready
battery_params the accepted plan has no battery parameters
plan_expired the original validity ended or no interval covers now
plan_malformed an interval has missing or invalid values; a new plan is required
operation_mode the inverter battery mode is neither Capacity nor Voltage
mode_not_commissioned the battery mode is not in commissioned_battery_modes (with the counter SOC estimator as the SOC source, Capacity never is)
voltage_range a Voltage-mode target outside 495–560 V
settings_range an entity range or step is missing, or a target is outside it
takeover_blocked an automation in old_writers is on or running
blueprint_active an automation using the Deye blueprint is on (see below); no write at all (not even the restore), and a repair issue names it
layout_mismatch the registers disagree with the entity states (see Supported hardware)
paused the pause switch is on
verification_required writes finished but not every register confirmed
write_failed a register did not confirm after retries
simulation_blocked Simulation refused while a restore was pending
run_failed the run raised an exception; details are in the Home Assistant log
controller_unavailable Energy Compass or the Solarman entities could not be read; nothing was written

Every runtime update of the blueprint engine goes through energy_compass.controller_runtime; when that call fails, the run stops before the next register is written. The native engine rejects that service, so a blueprint run that slips through stops before its first write.

Following a run (native engine)

The blueprint left an automation trace per run; the native engine replaces it with:

  • the runtime sensor's reason and reason_code, and its attribute last_run (not recorded): trigger, decision, planned commands, each write with its outcome (sent, failed, confirmed, blocked) and how the run ended;
  • the integration's diagnostics (deye_controller): engine, hardware, clock (clock_skew_seconds, clock_read_at, inverter_clock), grid (the sources, both times, the watch and the last 10 outage edges; with the planner's grid_outage_hold count under recalculation_cadence), run_history, the last 50 runs, and run_history_notable, the last 20 that wrote or ended with a code other than ok (both kept in memory, so a restart empties them);
  • a logbook entry on the runtime sensor whenever the runtime code or the confirmed mode changes;
  • the runtime code error and the repair issues "Deye controller runs are failing" and "Deye blueprint automation is still on", so a stopped controller is visible without reading logs;
  • the repair issue "Deye inverter clock is off by N min", when the inverter clock disagrees with Home Assistant time (Inverter clock).

When Energy Compass is unavailable

Without Energy Compass neither the mode nor the runtime can be read, so no write could be proven safe or recorded. The blueprint therefore stops at its first step, without any write or service call, when the controller sensor is missing or unavailable, reports another controller_schema or has no mode_entity: the trace says Energy Compass niedostępny: sterowanie wstrzymane bez zapisów. The native engine does the same without a trace: the run ends without a write, the runtime code is error with the reason controller_unavailable, and a repair issue appears after three such runs. The inverter keeps its last profile; a forced TOU direction ends at the next TOU program boundary, while the battery currents stay as they are. If Energy Compass disappears in the middle of a run, the next runtime call fails and the run stops before another register is written. Home Assistant reports the failed entry; repair it or release the inverter by hand.

Limits and defaults (native engine)

The expert group Limits and takeover of the options step sets these; an empty field keeps its default, and a change applies on the next run without a reload. No household value is built into the code.

Option Default
max_power_w the smaller of the charge and discharge power in the Energy Compass settings, in W
max_current, relinquish_current the max attribute of the charge-current entity, capped at max_power_w / 400 V
max_grid_current the max attribute of the grid-current entity, capped the same way
hold_grid_current, reached_discharge_current, balance_grid_current 1 A, 1 A, 2 A
min_buffer_current 1 A; the lowest charge or discharge current ever written outside the base profile; 0 allows 0 A again (expert opt-out)
grid_presence_entity the device's Solarman grid binary sensor (on = grid present)
grid_voltage_entities the device's grid_l1_voltage, grid_l2_voltage and grid_l3_voltage sensors
outage_enter_seconds 15 s (5–600): how long the grid must be absent before an outage is declared
outage_stable_minutes 5 min (1–120): how long it must be back before the outage ends
voltage_grid_charge_ceiling 55.2 V
commissioned_battery_modes Capacity
old_writers none
telemetry_entities the SOC and voltage sensors of the device
discharge_energy_entity the device's total battery discharge sensor when there is exactly one
entity overrides none; the six entities are found on the device by Solarman translation keys

When the power or a current limit would come out as zero (for example a charge power of 0 in the battery settings), the options step does not store it: it shows the group and asks you to enter the limits. Enabling the native engine also needs a numeric battery voltage reading, because the pack is told from a 48 V one by it. min_buffer_current must lie between 0 and the smaller of max_current and relinquish_current (controller_min_buffer_range), and the outage times in their ranges (controller_outage_range).

Inputs

These are the inputs of the deprecated blueprint, with the blueprint's own defaults; the native engine takes the values above.

Input Default Meaning
controller_entity — the Deye controller sensor of one Energy Compass installation (Options → Deye controller)
charge_entity, discharge_entity, grid_entity — battery max charging (108), max discharging (109) and grid charging (128) current
operation_entity — battery operation mode select (Capacity / Voltage)
soc_entity, voltage_entity — battery SOC (%) and pack voltage (V)
telemetry_entities — sensors that must be fresh (reported within 30 s)
max_power_w 8000 W battery power cap and TOU program power
max_current 18 A charge/discharge current cap in forced states
max_grid_current 16 A grid charging current cap
hold_grid_current 1 A charge and grid current in HOLD
balance_grid_current 2 A minimum grid current in an LFP balance row
reached_discharge_current 1 A discharge current after a DISCHARGE_GRID interval reached its target (direction Disabled, no selling)
relinquish_current 18 A charge/discharge current of the base profile
commissioned_battery_modes Capacity battery modes allowed for physical control
discharge_energy_entity none cumulative battery discharge energy (kWh); in Voltage mode ends DISCHARGE_GRID intervals on planned energy
voltage_grid_charge_ceiling 55.2 V TOU voltage for CHARGE_GRID in Voltage mode (49.5–56.0 V); the planned grid current carries the energy
old_writers none automations that must be off before any write

Capacity and the charge and discharge efficiencies are no longer inputs: the blueprint uses the values the accepted plan was computed with (capacity_kwh, eta_charge, eta_discharge), so a retained plan never runs with settings saved after it. max_power_w, max_current, max_grid_current and relinquish_current stay hardware caps in the blueprint; keep max_power_w consistent with the Energy Compass charge and discharge power, because the two are not linked.

Migrating from the package (0.1.36 and older)

Release 0.1.37 removes packages/energy_compass_deye.yaml. Energy Compass 0.1.36 and older ignore the controller options and store, so the controller needs 0.1.37 and the new blueprint together.

  1. Install 0.1.37 and restart. The controller is enabled automatically when the package helpers exist, there is one Energy Compass entry and one usable Solarman device; otherwise enable it in Options → Deye controller. The old blueprint and package keep controlling until you swap them.
  2. Optional shadow check. The controller sensor's generation should equal the state of the package's plan sensor after each acceptance.
  3. Compare efficiency and capacity first. The old blueprint used its own eta (default 0.9747) and capacity_kwh (default 25); the new one uses the plan's eta_charge, eta_discharge and capacity_kwh, which come from the Energy Compass battery settings (efficiency 1.0 unless set). Make eta_charge and eta_discharge equal to the old eta before the swap, or the first run rewrites the grid-charge and discharge currents by that ratio; a capacity difference moves only SOC thresholds, as below.
  4. Swap in a quiet window (a CHARGE_PV or SELF_CONSUME row, not near a full hour, with no other writer running). Turn the old automation off without stopping its actions, call energy_compass.controller_import_package for the controller sensor and check the answer (the package's session, accepted generation, mode and restore flag). It copies the state, adopts the package session and drops stale runtime keys. Then replace the blueprint, select the controller sensor in the automation, drop the eight removed inputs (plan_entity, optimizer_entity, valid_entity, alert_entity, compass_entity, solarman_device, capacity_kwh, eta) and turn it on. The first run changes nothing on the inverter when the capacity is unchanged; a capacity change moves only the active program's SOC and voltage threshold in a HOLD or grid row.
  5. Repoint dashboards and your own automations: the mode helper is now a select, the restore flag and the session are attributes, and the dashboard roles are deye_controller, deye_mode and deye_runtime.
  6. Remove the package include from configuration.yaml. It takes effect at the next restart; do not reload template or the input helpers meanwhile. Afterwards delete the ten orphaned registry entries.

Without the import, swap the blueprint anyway and accept one stretch on the base profile until the next plan. Rollback before the package is removed: turn the new automation off, restore the old blueprint and inputs and turn it on; the package helpers were never written by the import. A downgrade to 0.1.36 needs the old blueprint and the package back first.

Migrating from the blueprint to the native engine

The two engines never write together. Selecting native in Options → Deye controller → Engine is refused until the mode is Off and the restore is done. While the engine is native:

  • the mode select refuses to leave Off (the error names the automation) while an automation that uses the blueprint is on;
  • a run that would write (mode Auto, or Off with a restore pending) stops when such an automation is on: nothing is written, the runtime reason is blueprint_active (naming the automation) and a repair issue stays until the automation is switched off. Not even the restore to BASE is written meanwhile, so the inverter keeps the last profile it was given; once the automation is off, the controller continues (or restores BASE) on its next run. Mode Off with nothing to restore and Simulation run as usual and are not blocked. This also covers a reload with mode Auto and a blueprint that was never updated;
  • energy_compass.controller_runtime rejects every call, so a blueprint run that slips through stops before its first write.

When exactly one automation uses the blueprint on the same Solarman device (its charge, discharge, grid and operation entities belong to that device), its limits and entity overrides are loaded into the expert group for you to review; nothing is applied until you save. An automation on another inverter prefills nothing.

  1. Select the mode Off and wait until restore_pending is off and the runtime code is restored (or the run reports released).
  2. Turn the blueprint automation off. Do not stop its actions mid-run; wait for them to finish.
  3. Options → Deye controller: set the engine to native, review the prefilled limits and save. The entry reloads.
  4. Select Simulation, compare runtime.desired with what the blueprint wrote for a while, then select Auto in a CHARGE_PV or SELF_CONSUME row.
  5. After a week delete the automation and the blueprint file.

Rollback: select Off, wait for restored, set the engine to blueprint, turn the automation on, then choose the mode. A paused flag is cleared when the engine returns to blueprint.

Warning: the blueprint (frozen at 0.1.38) writes 0 A as the battery current limit in HOLD and has no outage state, so a rollback loses the grid outage safety: during an outage the battery may be disconnected from the house. Stay on the native engine on a site that can lose the grid.

Dashboard examples

Generated by tools/dashboards/build.py with placeholder entity IDs:

Section What it shows
controller_panel.yaml the controller at a glance: a Check control warning (stale forecast, Alert, runtime not ok, no fresh confirmation, unconfirmed writes), battery now with the mode selector and confirmed settings, the Compass decision with the controller's SOC target, the next 24 h of plan states with end SOC, a SOC forecast chart, the household consumption hint and cost, and 24 h history of SOC, power and control
controller_diagnostics.yaml optimizer and controller state, reason and reason code, the inverter and whether it is verified, the last run, confirmed mode, last confirmation, plan and forecast validity, active TOU program, unconfirmed writes, session and restore flags, and the read-back of the three current limits
plan_chart.yaml 12 h of measured load, grid, PV and SoC with the next 24 h of the plan over plan-state bands; grid-charge and grid-sell bands show the energy-weighted mean price of the block
consumer_compass_chart.yaml Consumer Compass levels, 4 h history and 20 h forecast

The panel uses native cards plus ApexCharts Card for its SOC forecast; the two charts need ApexCharts Card. The YAML builder fills any of them with your entity IDs, capacity and language. See the installation guide.

The controller examples take four roles: deye_controller, deye_mode, deye_runtime and deye_pause (defaults sensor.energy_compass_deye_controller, select.energy_compass_deye_mode, sensor.energy_compass_deye_controller_runtime and switch.energy_compass_pause_inverter_writes). The panel shows the pause switch only while the entity exists, that is with the native engine. Pass --entity deye_mode=select.my_mode to the generator or fill them in the YAML builder when your IDs differ; the session, the restore flag, the next TOU change and the TOU prefix are read from the controller's attributes.

Energy Atlas (optional)

Energy Atlas is a separate Datamindz service that aggregates anonymised telemetry across sites for research and benchmarking. Sending data to it is opt-in and off by default: with it off, Compass behaves and performs exactly as it does without this section — no network calls, no new background thread, no new files.

Turn it on in Settings → Devices & services → Energy Compass → Configure → Energy Atlas:

Field Meaning
Send to Energy Atlas Off by default.
Environment staging (atlas-api-staging.datamindz.io, for validating the data flow) or production (atlas-api.datamindz.io, the live collector). Staging validates the data flow; production is not available in this release yet (no credential baked in for it).
PV capacity (kWp) Installed PV capacity, entered once; not derived from other Compass settings. No default: required when sending is on.
Grid connection power (kW) Optional, 0.1–1000 kW: the site's grid connection limit, one value for import and export. Empty unless you saved one before — never prefilled from the grid import/export limits. Left empty, nothing is sent and the map counts the site as without max. Applies live like the rest of the form.

No secret to enter. This release registers with a shared public enrollment credential baked into the integration itself — the same one for every install of this version — so anyone running Energy Compass can register a site with it; the site is unverified until you send Energy Atlas: show ownership proof (below) to the Energy Atlas bot. The credential rotates by release: each new Compass version may ship a different one, and the old one is eventually revoked (already registered sites keep working — they authenticate by their own site key, not the enrollment credential).

Saving the form applies live: it does not reload the entry or touch your plan, and it starts or stops the delivery thread immediately. The form's description shows a status line so you can see it worked from your phone: off, or registered on <environment> · last delivery <time | never> · waiting <n> (plus halted: <kinds> if delivery is stuck).

What is sent, only while enabled and only the entities you have bound in Sources: PV, grid import/export and battery power, household load power (recorder mode only), battery SOC, and PV/import/export and battery charge/discharge energy counters (only counters whose Home Assistant state_class is total/total_increasing); each Compass solve's plan and its price/PV/load inputs; a handful of installation attributes (PV kWp, grid connection power in kW if you entered it, battery capacity and usable capacity, SOC floor, the Compass version) and the municipality (gmina) your Home Assistant home zone lies in, as its 7-digit id. Atlas shows the municipality by name next to your home's values. Compass finds the municipality inside Home Assistant: it reads the public outline files that Atlas serves (the same files for every home, found through GET /v1/public/geo) and compares them with your home's position there, so your coordinates stay in Home Assistant and no request carries them. The only things derived from them that leave are the voivodeship id in the name of the municipalities file Compass fetches and the municipality id in the attributes. A home within about 50 m of a municipal border may be shown in the neighbouring municipality, because the outlines are simplified. A home outside every Polish municipality (abroad, at sea) or without coordinates sends no location and is counted in the fleet total only. The files are fetched again only when Atlas publishes a new version or your home moves (Atlas is asked for the version at start and at most once per 24 h); if Atlas cannot be reached, the last municipality found is kept — also across a Home Assistant restart, in the integration's storage next to the site key together with the coordinates and the geometry version it was found for, never sent — and the lookup is retried at most once per hour, without ever delaying telemetry. Nothing else is sent — no tariff text or inverter model, and the enrollment credential itself is never stored, only the site key issued in exchange for it.

How values are sent: powers in W. Bind Battery power with + = discharge (as in the dashboard examples); Atlas receives it as + = charge. Readings outside the collector's ranges are corrected, not sent as errors: a negative grid import/export power is sent as 0, SOC below 0 % or above 100 % as 0 %/100 %, and a negative energy counter or a non-numeric reading is not sent.

Household load: Atlas receives the load power (load_w) from the optional Load power (Atlas telemetry only) source (measurement load_power, W or kW, with sign and maximum age like the other power sources), added in Configure → Sources. It is used only for Atlas, never by the load forecast or the optimizer, so a forecast from a long-term statistic (such as Solarman's lifetime consumption) can keep its long history and still feed Atlas. Without it Atlas uses the power entity of a Power history load source, as before. When it is set it is the only load reading sent (an unavailable or stale reading is not sent, there is no fallback to the load source). The history backfill follows the same rule.

Where the key lives: .storage/energy_compass_atlas/<entry id>/<environment>/ inside your Home Assistant config directory, one subdirectory per environment so staging and production never share a key, a site or a queue. It is included in Home Assistant backups. Removing the integration deletes it.

Switching environment: staging and production are independent — each keeps its own key, site and queued data. Switching to an environment that was already registered resumes it live (no reload, no re-registration, no lost queue); switching to one that has never been registered registers it automatically with the baked-in credential, without asking for anything.

When the collector is down: telemetry and solves queue locally (up to 30 days) and are sent once it is reachable again; Compass's own plan is unaffected — Atlas delivery runs on its own background thread and never shares the optimizer's schedule. Diagnostics (Devices & services → Energy Compass → ⋮ → Download diagnostics) report the energy_atlas section: enabled, environment, registration status, queue depth and any halted delivery.

Recovery: forget a site: if a site's key was revoked or conflicts with another source, check Forget site on this environment on the same Energy Atlas form and save. This deletes the selected environment's key and queued data on this device only — the site itself is not removed at the collector, an operator can revoke it separately — so the next save with sending still enabled registers a new site there automatically, again without asking for anything.

Show ownership proof: once a site is enabled and registered, the options menu offers an extra entry, Energy Atlas: show ownership proof. It generates a short-lived signed proof (valid 15 minutes, single use) and displays it to send to the Energy Atlas bot to link the site to your Datamindz account. The proof is shown only — it is never stored and never appears in options, diagnostics or logs.

Backfill history: the service Energy Atlas: backfill history (energy_compass.atlas_backfill, optional field Days, 1–3650, default: all available history) sends past telemetry from Home Assistant's own recorder history for every entity you have bound — 5-minute statistics where the recorder still keeps them, hourly statistics for older history — to every entry that currently has sending enabled and a registered site, using the same value corrections as live delivery. It fails with an error if no entry currently qualifies.

Offline replay tool

tools/replay.py answers "what does this setting change do to the real cost?" without Home Assistant. It imports the optimizer from custom_components/energy_compass/engine and replays recorded days; it needs the same Python and SciPy as the integration (run it in the test image or any environment where import scipy works) and plots nothing. For every day and in total it prints, in the installation's currency:

Column Cost of
plan the Energy Compass plan as executed: re-solved every refresh_minutes on the forecast known at plan time, the planned mode and energies applied to the realized PV and load
self_use plain self-consumption: the battery follows the load, no grid charging, no battery export
hindsight one solve of the same objective on the realized PV and load — the best the same settings could have done 
python tools/replay.py tools/replay_sample.json --currency PLN
python tools/replay.py tools/replay_sample.json --set allow_grid_charge=false

--set key=value (repeatable) overrides any planner setting by its key (the keys of Options, as in settings.py; strategy-owned flags set this way are treated as explicit). Run twice and compare the plan column to measure a change. --json prints the numbers (with solve_failures, the number of failed plan solves of the day) instead of the table; --timezone and --initial-soc apply to CSV input only. A bad file, value or override ends with error: … naming the place and exit code 2.

Input format

One JSON file (or a CSV, below). tools/replay_sample.json is a complete two-day synthetic example.

Key Meaning
timezone IANA name, e.g. Europe/Warsaw (default UTC)
interval_minutes interval length, default 15; all days of a file share it
settings optional planner settings (capacity_kwh, charge_kw, grid_export_kw, strategy, refresh_minutes, …); unset keys take the shipped defaults, so set at least the battery and site limits
days[].start ISO timestamp of the first interval (with offset, or local to timezone)
days[].date label for the table, default the local date of start
days[].initial_soc_percent battery SOC at start (default initial_soc_percent of the file, else 50)
days[].intervals[] one object per interval, in order and without gaps (below)

Each interval has six numbers: buy and sell (currency/kWh, the final tariff prices), pv_forecast and load_forecast (kWh in the interval, as known at plan time) and pv and load (kWh actually produced and consumed). The six values must be finite and the four energies not negative (clip the small negative values that rounding in statistics can leave, e.g. in import + PV − export); an error names the place, days[n][i] (day n from 1, interval i from 0) or line n of a CSV.

An interval may also carry buy_energy (CSV column too): the energy part of buy, the part the deposit can pay (the rest of buy is distribution), in the same units, as invoiced, so it may be negative (a draw at a negative energy price, dynamic offer without an index floor); it is not above max(buy, 0), and when negative not above buy; empty or missing means 0. The planner uses max(buy_energy, 0) (capped at max(buy, 0), as the engine does). It matters only with the deposit model, which you switch on with --set deposit_model=manual --set export_value_factor=0.3 (experimental). buy stays the invoice price, so buy_distribution_mode, buy_distribution_rate, buy_distribution_mid_peak_rate and buy_distribution_off_peak_rate are not read — prices come from the file — and a warning says so. Costs are reported at the file's prices whatever the factors are.

Days are independent: each is planned and measured on its own and ends at its last interval, even when the file holds consecutive days. The horizon therefore shrinks to the end of the day, so horizon_hours beyond the day and the carry of energy over midnight are not measured.

CSV has one row per interval with the columns start, buy, sell, pv_forecast, load_forecast, pv, load and optionally buy_energy and initial_soc_percent (read on the first row of a day). Rows are grouped into days by the local date of start; settings come only from --set.

Reading the result

  • Day-end energy is valued, because a day boundary is arbitrary for a battery. Every solve values the final SOC at terminal_value_per_kwh when terminal_mode is value, else at the day's mean buy price, so the plan may end a day below its initial SOC. The reported cost prices the difference between the final and the initial SOC at the day's mean buy price whatever the settings are, so terminal_mode and terminal_value_per_kwh change the plan but not the measuring stick: self_use is identical in every run, and two runs differing in the terminal value are comparable.
  • wear_per_kwh is part of the reported cost (half of the charged plus discharged energy), so runs with different wear_per_kwh are not comparable.
  • hindsight is the optimum of the shaped objective (strategy weights, import penalty and the terminal value of the solves included) priced in real currency. For cost_min with no import penalty and a terminal value equal to the day's mean buy price it is a lower bound of plan; for other strategies it is the best that strategy could do. With terminal_mode value and a lower value than the mean buy price, hindsight may drain the battery and report more than plan, which is a sign that the terminal value undervalues stored energy.
  • The executed plan follows the controller (tools/deye_controller/build.py) against realized data. SELF_CONSUME and CHARGE_PV follow the load: all PV surplus charges the battery and a deficit is covered from it. In CHARGE_GRID only the grid share follows the plan — the planned charge minus the surplus the forecast promised. Grid and the realized PV surplus charge together until the row's planned end SOC; then the grid stops, as the controller does, and PV keeps charging for the rest of the slot. PV above the forecast therefore shrinks the grid import (the SOC may end above plan, by PV only), and PV below it charges less — a shortfall is never bought from the grid, nor a start SOC below plan caught up. DISCHARGE_GRID discharges the planned energy, HOLD parks the battery. Grid export beyond grid_export_kw is curtailed, and stored energy is not exported beyond the PV produced so far when Sell only PV (limit_export_to_pv) is on.
  • On a net-metering file the costs are hourly prices, not the settlement. Net-metering is settled on yearly kWh (Setup profiles), so plan − self_use is not a saving there; do not compare strategies by it.
  • The peak-period reserve (peak_reserve_margin_kwh and export_reserve_margin_kwh) is replayed as in the integration: it needs limit_grid_charge_price (its ceiling is the cheap price), else a warning says it has no effect.
  • Not replayed: LFP balance windows, the autonomy tail beyond the data, and carried export or grid-charge commitments. A warning names the enabled ones. A failed plan solve runs that step as self-consumption and is reported under the table and as solve_failures; a failed hindsight solve or inconsistent settings stop the run with error: <date>: ….

Exporting the data from Home Assistant

buy and sell are the final prices the planner sees: from your tariff, or from the history of the price entities Energy Compass reads. The realized energy comes from long-term statistics: the Energy dashboard's menu offers Download data (CSV, hourly). The same hourly change values the replay needs are returned by the recorder/statistics_during_period WebSocket command with "period": "hour" and "types": ["change"] (tools/export_value_backfill.py shows the call). Take pv from the PV production statistic and load from the home consumption statistic (energy in = grid import + PV − grid export, when no consumption sensor exists). pv_forecast and load_forecast are what your forecast entities said before the interval — the Compass plan attribute intervals (or the Solcast/forecast history) recorded at plan time; using the realized value as the forecast gives an idealised plan with no forecast error. Use interval_minutes: 60 for hourly statistics.

Annual settlement oracle

tools/replay_year.py is the yearly counterpart of the day replay, for the questions a day cannot answer: what a deposit setting does to the bill of a year. It replays consecutive hours as the integration runs them: a receding horizon_hours (24 h) window, re-planned every --refresh-hours hours (default 6) on the forecast, the state of charge carried over midnight, the daily PV-export counters reset at local midnight, every plan executed on the realized series, a failed solve run as self-consumption. The hourly import and export it produces are valued by two bills:

Bill Rule
annual the deposit D = 1.23 × V (V = value of the exported energy at max(sell, 0)) pays the liability E⁺ = Σ max(Et, 0) of the monthly energy parts Et of the imports; the refund is min(D − min(D, E⁺), ρ × V). A month with a negative energy part (dynamic price without an index floor, charging in negative-price hours) owes nothing and never feeds the deposit: it stays on the bill at full value, never refunded, capped or voided (ADR-0031 Amendment T-471). So bill = fixed + Σ import × buy − applied − refund, and the signed energy part (a negative month included) is inside Σ import × buy
ledger the deposit of every month is a vintage booked the following month, paid out oldest first, usable for 12 months; at expiry min(unused, ρ × V of the month) comes back and the rest is void. It is the steady state of a repeated year: D ≤ E⁺ gives the annual result, D > E⁺ a warm-up year from a full account (every live vintage at its whole deposit) and then the measured year 
python tools/replay_year.py site.json --set deposit_model=manual --set export_value_factor=0.3
python tools/replay_year.py site.csv --timezone Europe/Warsaw --rho 0.2 --fixed 310 --self-use

It prints (or, with --json, returns) both bills, wear, the SOC drift (initial minus final SOC at the mean buy price), K = annual bill + wear + SOC drift (KL with the ledger), D, V, E (signed), E_owed (E⁺; the text output labels it E+ liability), and the refund and the void of each bill. Compare two runs by the difference of K (or KL); --self-use gives the no-planner reference. The input is one JSON object (timezone, start, rho, fixed, initial_soc_percent, settings and hours[]) or a CSV, one row per hour with start, buy, sell, buy_energy, pv_forecast, load_forecast, pv, load — the same values as above; the format is in the tool's docstring, --rho, --fixed and --initial-soc override the file. buy_energy is the energy part as invoiced, with its sign: the bills sum it per month (a draw at a negative energy price lowers the month, and a month that ends below zero stays in the bill at full value and adds nothing to E_owed), while the planner sees max(buy_energy, 0), so the plan does not depend on the negative values. Hours must be consecutive real hours, one row each; a JSON row may carry its own start, which must then match its position. --refresh-hours must not exceed horizon_hours. The number of failed plan solves is printed on stderr in both output formats.

Timestamps are real instants, so a year across the two clock changes (a 25-hour and a 23-hour local day) is read correctly; the local date and month (counter reset, ledger month) come from timezone. A stamp with an offset (+02:00, Z) is exact. A naive stamp is local to timezone: in the repeated autumn hour it is the first occurrence, unless the row before it is that first occurrence (then it is the second), so a CSV of consecutive naive local stamps reads right — a naive JSON start in that hour is the first occurrence; give it an offset to mean the second.

Limits: the fixed part of the bill is one number from the input and does not follow the flow, so a charge band that depends on the annual import is not modelled (take fixed from the no-battery bill and expect a small constant error where the band differs); a stretch shorter than a year is read as a year with empty months; the settlement period is the calendar month; a seller that bills a longer period nets across its months, which the tool does not model; energy is valued per hour; the result is only as good as the forecast series you give it.

Reason code reference

Coverage / quality reasons (reason, reasons attributes)

Code Meaning
complete Full reference coverage, all probes succeeded.
available_reference_horizon Source coverage shorter than the requested reference horizon; percentiles use what exists.
reference_horizon_uncovered Reserved in translations; not emitted by 0.1.45.
reference_probe_failed At least one reference probe failed or timed out.
short_source_coverage Price/forecast coverage ends before the requested planning horizon.
current_guidance_unavailable Current interval probe unknown; later windows may still be valid.
missing_forecast_continuation A configured source (except the optional pessimistic PV source) has not yet published data for part of the requested horizon (e.g. tomorrow's prices before ~14:00).
load_history_fallback Part of the load forecast uses the fallback daily load because history is insufficient.
unvalidated_tariff Tariff calibration marked unvalidated.
unvalidated_capacity Battery capacity calibration marked unvalidated.

Autonomy warnings

Code Meaning
autonomy_floor_requires_pv No PV source — floor skipped.
autonomy_tail_coarsened 48 h tail longer than 192 intervals, coarsened to hourly.
autonomy_tail_unavailable Tail source failed; floor uses the priced horizon only.
grid_charge_ceiling_below_autonomy_weight Grid-charge ceiling below floor weight − margin; floor could never be refilled.
peak_reserve_requires_grid_charge_ceiling peak_reserve_margin_kwh above 0 but Limit grid-charging price off — peak-period reserve skipped.
peak_reserve_inactive No upcoming expensive run with a deficit in the horizon — peak-period reserve has nothing to protect.
export_reserve_requires_grid_charge_ceiling export_reserve_margin_kwh above 0 but Limit grid-charging price off — buffer under an export skipped.
export_reserve_requires_battery_export export_reserve_margin_kwh above 0 but battery export off — buffer under an export skipped.

Safety exceptions (dispatch_policy.safety_exception.reason)

Code Meaning
observed_soc_maximum Charging commitment active but SOC already at the maximum.
observed_soc_minimum Discharge commitment active but SOC at or below the reserve (a carried SELF_CONSUME only when its release from the empty pack has no plan).
grid_charge_price_limit Carried CHARGE_GRID would continue above the grid-charge price ceiling.

Balance warnings

These are raw codes, not translated.

Code Meaning
balance_overdue The balance phase is due but no hold window could be fit into the plan; a balance was missed this horizon.
balance_pessimistic_pv_unavailable A pessimistic PV source is configured but unavailable, stale, malformed or negative, or does not cover the horizon; the balance windows were chosen on the median PV series.
balance_no_window_in_horizon The balance phase is eligible or due but no candidate hold window exists in the horizon at all (no aligned start satisfies PV/grid-charge feasibility).
